strategy.summary: Reproduce astropy/astropy#18348 regression where astropy.convolution.convolve produces NaN “buffer” / inconsistent NaN treatment vs astropy.convolution.convolve_fft. The transition is the added regression test test_regression_16497_nan_treatment_consistency failing on buggy commit ed0072408b14 and passing on the fixed revision.

strategy.reproducing_test:
The regression test exactly as added in astropy/convolution/tests/test_convolve.py:
- Uses convolve and convolve_fft with boundary='fill', fill_value=np.nan, preserve_nan=True.
- First checks equality when the input array has no NaNs (ar=np.ones((10,10))).
- Then injects a single NaN at ar[5,5]=np.nan and checks that exactly one NaN appears in each output and that convolve and convolve_fft match.
strategy.success_criterion:
On the buggy revision (astropy commit ed0072408b14), test_regression_16497_nan_treatment_consistency fails: either (a) assert_array_almost_equal(result_convolve, result_convolve_fft, decimal=10) fails for the no-NaN input case, and/or (b) the finite-ness assertions fail because convolve outputs NaNs even though the input contains no NaNs.
On the fixed revision, the test passes: both convolutions match to decimal=10 for the no-NaN input case and both results are finite; for the single-NaN case, smoothed and smoothed_fft each have exactly one NaN at/only around the NaN position and match to decimal=10.
strategy.numerical_probe: The test’s probe is structural/numerical: it asserts exact finiteness (no NaNs) for the all-ones input when boundary fill uses fill_value=np.nan, and uses assert_array_almost_equal(..., decimal=10) to ensure convolve and convolve_fft are consistent. Then it checks np.sum(np.isnan(output))==1 after setting ar[5,5]=np.nan and convolve and convolve_fft match.

input_output_examples.input: ar = np.ones((10, 10)) ; gaussian = Gaussian2DKernel(1, x_size=5, y_size=5) ; convolve(ar, gaussian, boundary='fill', fill_value=np.nan, preserve_nan=True)
input_output_examples.expected_output: result_convolve should be finite (no NaNs) and equal to convolve_fft(... ) within decimal=10; also convolve and convolve_fft should match exactly at decimal=10.

input_output_examples.input: ar = np.ones((10, 10)); ar[5, 5]=np.nan ; gaussian = Gaussian2DKernel(1, x_size=5, y_size=5) ; preserve_nan=True ; boundary='fill' ; fill_value=np.nan
input_output_examples.expected_output: smoothed and smoothed_fft should each have exactly one NaN: np.sum(np.isnan(smoothed))==1 and np.sum(np.isnan(smoothed_fft))==1, and smoothed matches smoothed_fft within decimal=10.

risks: This defect may depend on specific convolution implementation details in the affected astropy revision; ensure you run the exact test from the buggy tree (including the added regression test).

If the fixed revision is not located and you only test against PyPI wheels, you may not transition; you must build/run the astropy commit ed0072408b14 and the known fixed commit. The environment pins numpy/scipy/astropy per CONTEXT but do not replace the need to run the repo code at the specified commits.

The reproduction is unlikely to vary by platform, but numeric FFT/back-end differences (FFTW availability, MKL, CPU architecture) can affect decimal=10 comparisons; if the transition still doesn’t occur, run on the same platform/CI image where the regression was observed or force a consistent FFT provider.
The evidence only grounds NaN handling; do not assume failures for other special values (e.g., +/-inf).

oracle.reference_source: Internal cross-check: the test uses equality between astropy.convolution.convolve and astropy.convolution.convolve_fft within decimal=10, plus finiteness/NaN-count invariants.
oracle.why: No standalone numeric ground truth is provided in the evidence; the correctness oracle is the consistency between the two APIs and the expected NaN-count/finite behavior described in issue #16497 and encoded in the regression test.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion that should fail is the test’s transition check: for ar=np.ones((10,10)), result_convolve will contain NaNs and/or differ from result_convolve_fft, causing either assert np.all(np.isfinite(result_convolve)) / assert np.all(np.isfinite(result_convolve_fft)) to fail and/or assert_array_almost_equal(result_convolve, result_convolve_fft, decimal=10) to fail. For the single-NaN case, convolve may keep more NaNs than expected or disagree with convolve_fft, failing the np.sum(np.isnan(...))==1 and/or the final assert_array_almost_equal(smoothed, smoothed_fft, decimal=10).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed revision ensures that with no NaNs in the input, convolve and convolve_fft both return finite outputs matching to decimal=10; with a single NaN at ar[5,5], both outputs contain exactly one NaN and match to decimal=10.
